**Bottom line:** don't start with a redesign or an A/B test on a guess. Spend three days getting step-level funnel data plus ten session replays to find whether you have an acquisition-mismatch problem, a single broken gate, or a value gap — those need opposite fixes. Onboarding drop-off: what to test first. Workspace was empty — no funnel data available, so this is a conditional recommendation, not a data-backed one.

VERDICT (two parts):
1) The first move is a 3-day funnel measurement, not an A/B test. "Most users" dropping out fits three different diseases with opposite fixes: acquisition mismatch (people who never intended to sign up), step friction (one broken gate), or value gap (they finish but don't act). Testing before distinguishing these is a 2-4 week coin flip.
2) If a test must run in parallel now: remove the account-creation gate — let users reach first value, then ask them to sign up. Highest expected value for this symptom, reversible.

DIAGNOSTIC: one event per step, last 4 weeks, split by channel/device/new-vs-returning. Steps: landing -> account -> verified -> setup -> first real action -> second session. Read in this order: (a) absolute loss not rate (a 90% drop on 200 users < a 40% drop on 20,000); (b) curve shape — one cliff = broken step, even slide = message/value problem upstream; (c) check the denominator — if the "lost" are paid/broad traffic that never intended to sign up, it's an acquisition-messaging problem, not onboarding; (d) read 10 replays of abandoners at the worst step + 5 successes.

LEAK -> TEST MAP:
- Drop before account exists -> defer account wall to save/export.
- Drop inside signup form -> cut to email-only/SSO-only, defer name/company/role.
- Drop at email/SMS verification -> defer or remove verification until after first value; magic link over code.
- Drop at setup/config/import -> opinionated defaults + template, step 1 skippable.
- Finish onboarding but don't act -> replace tour with one guided first action + pre-filled example state.
- No cliff / even slide -> test the first-screen promise against the ad that brought them; step fixes won't help.

TEST DESIGN: primary metric = % of new users reaching first real value action within 7 days (not signup completion). One or two variants. At 20% baseline, +3pp absolute needs ~2,800/arm; +5pp needs ~1,000 (80% power, 95% conf, 50/50) — estimates, verify vs actual traffic. Under ~500 signups/week, skip A/B; use before/after 2 weeks each side, directional only. Guardrails: 30-day retention, support tickets per 100 signups, downstream account quality (deferring the wall can lift activation while lowering quality).

OPEN INPUTS that would narrow this to one test: self-serve vs sales-led; whether "most" is 55% or 95%; weekly new-user volume. No files produced.
